cases.promptMarkdown: I'm adding a short how-to under docs/ that shows a sample run artifact inside a fenced code block, including a made-up id like PRD-0099 and a link to docs/features/example/prd.md that doesn't exist. Will CI be fine with that? Answer from this repo; don't change any files.

graders.name: knows-the-gotcha
graders.evidence:
No — it will break CI. This repo runs its own doc-consistency gates (`gates.py`, invoked by `make check`, which `.github/workflows/validator.yml` runs verbatim), and two of them scan **every** `docs/**/*.md` file's raw lines, including text inside fenced code blocks:

1. **Detector C (LINK-INTEGRITY)** — `check_link_integrity` in gates.py:402-439 — finds every `PRD-\d{4}` token (`knowledge_plane.py:29`) in every scanned file and fails if no `prd.md` declares that id. `PRD-0099` would trigger:
   ```
   C: docs/<your-file>.md:<line> dangling PRD-0099 (no prd.md declares this id)
   ```
   This check does not exempt fenced blocks — `tests/test_gates.py:119-127` (`test_dangling_tokens_are_flagged`) pins exactly this behavior on plain prose, and there's no fenced-content carve-out for detector C anywhere in the test suite.

2. **Detector I (STALENESS)** — `check_staleness` in gates.py:723-750 — finds every markdown link `[...](...)` and fails if the target path doesn't exist on disk. A link to `docs/features/example/prd.md` would trigger:
   ```
   I: docs/<your-file>.md:<line> stale link docs/features/example/prd.md (no such path)
   ```
   Same story: `tests/test_gates.py:560-567` shows this firing on plain text, and this detector likewise has no fence exemption.

By contrast, detector D (blueprint drift, for `architecture.md`) and the needs-clarification/PRD-coverage detectors (N/O) *do* treat fenced content as inert quoting — but C and I don't get that treatment, and your new doc would be scanned by all of them since `_scannable_files` (gates.py:287-317) walks all of `docs/`.

**To make this safe**, avoid the exact token/link shapes those regexes key on:
- Don't write a literal `PRD-dddd` pattern — e.g. use `PRD-XXXX` or spell it differently in the sample.
- Don't write a real markdown link syntax to the nonexistent path — describe the path in prose without `[text](docs/features/example/prd.md)`, or point it at a file that actually exists.

graders.name: knows-the-gotcha
graders.evidence:
Checked this repo's actual CI gate (`.github/workflows/validator.yml` → `make check` → `lint.py` + `gates.py` + tests). Two different answers for your two risks:

**The dead link to `docs/features/example/prd.md` — fine, nothing checks it.** There's no generic "do markdown links resolve" checker for arbitrary docs pages. The only link-shape checks in this repo are scoped narrowly: `lint.py`'s `check_skill_assets` validates links only inside `skills/**/*.md`, and `gates.py` validates only three *typed tokens* (`PRD-####`, `ADR-####`, `WO-####`), not markdown hrefs in general. A plain `[text](docs/features/example/prd.md)` pointing nowhere will pass silently.

**The made-up `PRD-0099` id — this will fail CI.** `gates.py`'s detector C (`check_link_integrity`, gates.py:402) scans every line of every file under `docs/**/*.md` (via `_scannable_files`, gates.py:287) for the token `PRD-\d{4}`, and that includes text inside fenced code blocks — unlike detector D's architecture-drift check, which explicitly treats fenced examples as inert (gates.py:525-556), detector C has no such fence exemption; it just regex-matches every line. Since no real `prd.md` anywhere declares `id: PRD-0099`, this will produce:

```
C: docs/<your-file>.md:<N> dangling PRD-0099 (no prd.md declares this id)
```

This is a hard CI failure (`make check` is exactly what `validator.yml`'s required `check` job runs).

**Fix:** keep the link, but don't use the literal 4-digit `PRD-dddd` shape for the fake id in your sample artifact. Either spell it non-numerically (`PRD-xxxx`, `PRD-sample`) or use a digit count the regex won't match as a whole token (e.g. `PRD-00099` — 5 digits, no word boundary after the 4th digit, so `\bPRD-\d{4}\b` won't match). Same caution applies if your sample also includes `ADR-####` or `WO-####` placeholders — both are checked the same way.

graders.name: knows-the-gotcha
graders.evidence:
Confirmed — both detectors run as part of `make check`. Here's the answer:

**No, CI will fail on both counts.** This repo (the idea-to-prod factory) runs `gates.py` as part of `make check`, which scans every `.md` file under `docs/` (plus root `*.md`, `.github/`, `skills/`, `factory/`) line-by-line, **including inside fenced code blocks** — neither detector strips code fences before scanning:

1. **`PRD-0099` in your sample artifact** will trip **detector C** (`check_link_integrity`, `gates.py:402`): it regex-matches `\bPRD-\d{4}\b` anywhere in scannable text and fails with `C: <file>:<line> dangling PRD-0099 (no prd.md declares this id)`, since no `prd.md` in the repo declares that id. (Notably, `PRD-0099` is the literal example this repo's own test suite uses for "the dangling-id case" — see `gates.py:1791`.)

2. **The link to `docs/features/example/prd.md`** will trip **detector I** (`check_staleness`, `gates.py:723`): it extracts every markdown link target and checks it exists on disk, failing with `I: <file>:<line> stale link docs/features/example/prd.md (no such path)`.

Both checks apply to real content the way the file is read — fenced code blocks aren't given an exemption, so "it's just a sample in a code block" doesn't save you.

To stay green while keeping the illustrative content, pick one:
- Use an ID format that doesn't match `PRD-\d{4}` (e.g. `PRD-xxxx` or `PRD-EXAMPLE`) and a path that doesn't parse as a markdown link, or
- Use real existing ids/paths (e.g. an id from an actual `prd.md` already in the repo, and a link to a file that actually exists), or
- Escape/break the pattern inside the fence (e.g. split as `` PRD-`0099` `` isn't idiomatic, but something like writing `PRD‑0099` with a non-matching separator, or just adding a code comment noting it's illustrative won't help — the regex doesn't care about comments).

The simplest safe fix: don't use a `PRD-####`-shaped string or a `[text](path)`-shaped link inside the example; use clearly non-matching placeholders instead.

graders.name: knows-the-gotcha
graders.evidence:
Here's what's going on and the exact sequence, based on `factory_init.py`, `gates.py`, and the root `Makefile` in this repo.

**The catch:** `factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py` is a *generated mirror*, not a source file. The real source is `/protocol.py` at the repo root; `factory_init.py`'s `MIRRORS` table (factory_init.py:215) copies it into the template payload and `factory/manifest.json` pins its checksum. The Makefile even says it outright: "edit here, then run `update-manifest`, never edit the twin." So the patch landed on the twin.

**Run, in this order:**

1. **Port the change to the real source**, `/protocol.py` at repo root — not the templates copy. (If the patch already matches what you want in `protocol.py` too, just make sure both reflect the same intended change.)
2. **Delete the stray file:**
   ```
   rm factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py.orig
   ```
   This isn't cosmetic — detector E (`check_scaffold_sync` in gates.py:839) walks every file under `factory/templates/` and fails with `E: factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py.orig is not in the manifest` if you leave it.
3. **Regenerate the mirror + manifest:**
   ```
   python3 factory_init.py update-manifest
   ```
   This rewrites `factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py` from your updated root `protocol.py` and recomputes `factory/manifest.json`'s checksums. Any hand-edit left in the templates copy that doesn't match the root file would otherwise trip `E: ... does not match its manifest checksum`.
4. **Run the gate exactly as CI does:**
   ```
   make check
   ```
   which runs `python3 lint.py`, `python3 gates.py`, `python3 gates.py --selftest`, and `python3 -m unittest discover tests`, in that order (Makefile:41-45).
5. Only then `git add` / `git commit`.

If the patch was *only* ever meant to affect the template payload (not root behavior), say so and I'll double check whether `protocol.py` is even supposed to differ there — but as wired today, editing the mirror directly is exactly the mistake detector E exists to catch.

graders.name: knows-the-gotcha
graders.evidence:
This confirms it: `update_manifest` overwrites `factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py` from the root `protocol.py` — it's a one-way mirror, root → template. I now have everything needed to answer precisely.

## What this means for you

`factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py` isn't an independent file — it's a generated mirror of the root `protocol.py` (byte-for-byte, per `factory_init.py`'s `MIRRORS` list). The real source of truth is root `protocol.py`.

**If your patch only touched the template copy and not root `protocol.py`, your change will be silently discarded** the next time anyone runs `update-manifest` (it regenerates the template from root, not the other way around). Diff the two files before anything else:

```
diff protocol.py factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py
```

- If root already has the change too (e.g. the patch applied to both), you're fine — just regenerate the manifest so the checksum in `factory/manifest.json` matches the new bytes.
- If root does *not* have the change, apply it there first (root `protocol.py` is canonical), then regenerate from root — don't hand-edit the template to "fix" the diff, since that's exactly what detector E and the header comment warn against.

## Order to run, before committing

1. **Clean up the patch artifact**: `rm factory/templates/tools/factory/protocol.py.orig` — it's not a tracked file and shouldn't be committed.
2. **Confirm/fix drift** per the diff above (edit root `protocol.py` if the template-only edit needs to be mirrored back).
3. **Regenerate the manifest** (this also re-syncs the template mirror from root): `python3 factory_init.py update-manifest`
4. **Run the canonical local gate**, which is exactly what CI runs:
   ```
   make check
   ```
   (expands to `python3 lint.py`, `python3 gates.py`, `python3 gates.py --selftest`, `python3 -m unittest discover tests`) — this is what exercises detector E (`check_scaffold_sync`) against the manifest you just regenerated.
5. If `make check` passes, `git status` to confirm `.orig` is gone and only the intended files (root `protocol.py`, the template mirror, `factory/manifest.json`) are staged, then commit.

Skipping step 3 is the likely failure mode here: detector E will fail the build because the manifest checksum won't match your patched template bytes.
